rationale: bugs_open/170 was filed as a READ defect: the style_collections chrome pin (header_component_id/footer_component_id) is dereferenced by GetComponentByID, whose SQL is `WHERE id = $1` with no predicate, so RenderHeader/RenderFooter render whatever is pinned. That is true and re-verified live on 2026-08-01. But the filing's own framing — 'a fourth path that 118's three-call-site census did not include' — hid the half that matters. THE PIN IS ALSO A WRITE SOURCE. LinkSiteComponentsAction reads scol.header_component_id / scol.footer_component_id and calls ResolveChromeComponent (the eligible-only pool lookup bugs_closed/118 installed) ONLY when the pin is NULL; a pin that is present is used unconditionally and handed to relinkSiteComponent, which upserts it into site_components.component_id and sets rendered_html = NULL, build_status = 'pending'. So an unguarded pin does not merely render a deactivated component — it OVERWRITES the repair bugs_closed/166 performed on the same column, in the same slot, for the same sites. And fork_theme_from_site COPIES the parent collection's pins into a new collection with no check, which is how the bad state propagates to collections that do not have it yet. Three consumers, one unguarded dereference, none of them aware of the predicate the rest of chrome selection shares. MEASURED LIVE 2026-08-01: four style collections carry pins; three sites are pinned to header-professional-dark (is_active=false) and FOUR to footer-4-column (is_active=false) — the footer count is one higher than 170 records, because leopardessconsulting.co.uk's header pin is the fleet's one legitimate pin while its footer pin is not. Every one of those sites' site_components assignments is already CORRECT (header-theme-chrome / footer-theme-chrome / header-leopardess), repointed on 2026-07-31. The two stores now disagree in writing, and the unguarded one wins on both the render and the write path. WHY THIS IS NOT THE OWNER CALL 170 WAS WAITING FOR. 170 held candidate 1 back because it 'changes served markup on three live sites'. Re-read against what 166 actually shipped, that does not survive: guarding the pin makes those sites fall through to ResolveChromeComponent, which returns header-theme-chrome / footer-theme-chrome — exactly the components 166 already moved the same sites' assignments to, with council approval, live today. The change does not decide anything new about how those sites look; it makes the pin path agree with the answer the platform has already given. That is a judgement and it is stated as one, not smuggled. THE PREDICATE IS REUSED, NOT INVENTED. chromePinEligibleSQL is the 167 lane's own predicate, written in its council round 1 and deleted in round 3 (2605d3f92) together with the per-render reporter it fed. Four seats rejected THE REPORTER; the predicate was not the objection, and it arrived with a live measurement over all four pins that is why it is right. It omits `forked_from IS NULL`, which the POOL predicate carries: a fork is illegitimate as a library default (118's header-leopardess finding) and is the entire point of a pin. Re-measured 2026-08-01, the two predicates disagree on exactly one live row and the pin predicate is the one that gets it right — copying chromeEligibleSQL here would delete the single correct pin in the fleet while still catching the three wrong ones. The architecture seat objected in 167 round 2 that this was 'a SECOND bespoke eligibility predicate'. The answer is that a predicate feeding one zap.Logger call on one path is bespoke, whereas one named predicate that every pin consumer dereferences through is what turns three hand-written pin reads into one; the test of 'bespoke' is how many callers it serves. WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO, stated rather than discovered in review. (1) It does not repair the four style_collections rows — they still name ineligible components; every consumer now ignores them, which is why edit 4 files a work item so the rows are visible and queryable instead of merely inert. (2) It does not change any live page today: chrome is a stored artefact and no page re-render regenerates it (bugs_open/117), so served markup moves only on the next chrome rebuild. (3) The `component_level` clause of the pin predicate is INERT against today's data — all four ineligible pins fail on is_active alone; it is a forward guard against 167's class arriving through a pin, not a clause doing work now. (4) The diagnosis loop was run on this mechanism (090, correlation ce9bcd92-7be7-4819-bdf8-f8a57622128f) and COMPLETED WITHOUT A VERDICT: component_library.go is 93,905 bytes and the bundle body cap is 60,000, so the one symbol the run needed was omitted from all four iterations ('0 of 1 in-scope symbol(s) rendered with a body'). Its independent live query did reproduce the 3-header/4-footer count exactly. First-hand verification was substituted and is described in the bug file. CONSUMERS TOLD, per the owner ruling of 2026-07-29 point 3: the mechanisms whose guarantee changes are (a) link_site_components / the site-component-linker agent — a pinned component is no longer automatically what the slot is linked to; if the pin is ineligible the slot now gets the library's eligible chrome instead, which is the behaviour a NULL pin already had; (b) fork_theme_from_site — a forked collection now inherits only eligible pins, and inherits NULL otherwise, which is what install_site_composition already does at install; (c) deactivated_site_components — its population grows to include pins, filing 7 items fleet-wide today, none of them for the one legitimate pin.

plan.summary: Give the style_collections chrome pin the one predicate the rest of chrome selection already shares, at all three consumers that dereference it (render, link, fork), and extend the existing deactivated_site_components detector to see pins so a wrong row is visible rather than merely ignored. The pin predicate is deliberately NOT the pool predicate: it omits forked_from IS NULL, because pinning a site to its own fork is what a pin is for. Two static guards keep it that way — a scan that fails on any unguarded pin dereference in the actions package, and a lockstep that fails if the detector's hand-typed copy of the predicate drifts from the shared one (discovery_checks cannot import actions; the dependency runs the other way).

edits.rationale: The shared pin predicate and the ONE way to dereference a pin, plus the two render call sites routed through it. GetChromePinComponent returns (component, eligible, error) — the same shape as ResolveChromeComponent, so the two read alike at a call site — and the eligibility flag rides on the SAME query that fetches the row, so a caller cannot be told the component is fine by one round trip and the truth by another. An ineligible pin leaves comp nil and falls through to the existing by-function branch, i.e. the eligible-only pool lookup 167 fixed. Deliberately NOT a change to GetComponentByID: that is a general by-id fetch used by RenderComponentAction to render arbitrary page sections, where a chrome-level predicate would be wrong — and the scan in edit 5 is written so it does not fire on that call.

The write half, and the reason this is urgent rather than cosmetic. The pins now arrive WITH their eligibility, decided by the same query that reads them, and an ineligible pin is DISCARDED — which hands the slot to the eligible-only library lookup immediately below, the path a collection with no pin already takes. Discarding rather than refusing is deliberate: refusing would leave the slot pointing at whatever it already holds. Two aliases (hc./fc.) in one query is also why the predicate function takes an alias — an unqualified column here would resolve to whichever table the planner chose.

The propagation path, found by the scan in edit 5 rather than by reading — which is the argument for the scan. Forking copies the parent collection's pins into a NEW collection unconditionally, so forking professional-dark today manufactures a fresh collection pinned to header-professional-dark and footer-4-column, both is_active=false: new instances of the defect, not a repeat of an old one. An ineligible pin now arrives NULL, which is not a loss — a collection with no pin takes the by-function branch and gets the library's eligible chrome, exactly as install_site_composition_action leaves both columns NULL at install. chromePinEligibleSQL and not chromeEligibleSQL matters most here: this is the action most likely to meet a legitimate fork.

edits.rationale: 170's candidate 1b, and the reuse-shaped half: the detector for this exact defect class exists, fires, and joins site_components ONLY — so for its whole life it has been blind to half its own subject, which is why three deployed sites had no work item and no finding. A second query over sites -> style_collections -> content_components, in the same check, reusing the same deactivated_component item type and triage path. Three traps handled explicitly: (a) item_key is deactivated_PIN_<slot>, because dedup is UNIQUE (site_id, item_key) over non-terminal statuses and the assignment item already keys on deactivated_<slot> for the same slot on the same site — a shared key would silently swallow whichever was filed second; (b) NO handler_agent — rerender-pages re-renders and cannot write a style_collections row, so routing this at it files an item unsatisfiable by construction, which is bugs_open/166 reproduced on a new item type; repointing a SHARED collection (professional-dark serves three sites) is a decision, so it is needs_human_review; (c) the verifier_coverage_test contract that deactivated_component items 'all carry component_id' still holds — a pin item carries the pinned component's id — and the suite is green. MEASURED: it files exactly 7 items fleet-wide today, 3 header + 4 footer, and zero for leopardess's legitimate header pin.

edits.rationale: The door, plus the behaviour. The scan is the framework-level half: the three consumers did not disagree with the eligibility rule on purpose, they were each written separately against a general-purpose by-id fetch and nothing connected them — a fourth written tomorrow would do the same. It matches both original forms (the Go dereference and the raw SQL pin read) and is proven by induction: a synthetic fifth consumer carrying both forms COMPILES CLEANLY and is caught at both, and removing it goes green. It is also proven NOT to fire on RenderComponentAction's legitimate general by-id fetch. The behaviour tests cover the fallback AND the positive control an eligible pin must still be honoured with no library lookup at all, without which the whole change is satisfied by ignoring pins entirely. NOTE A CORRECTION CARRIED IN THE FILE: the scan's first version reported link_site_components — the file this fix had just corrected — as an offender, because the sanctioned guarded form injects the predicate by concatenation so component_level appears in NEITHER string literal. It now stitches the Go glue back in, statement-locally rather than file-wide, and a fixture proves the stitching is what does the work.

The detector's copy of the predicate is hand-typed, and it has to be: actions imports discovery_checks to register the checks, so discovery_checks cannot import chromePinEligibleSQL back. Two hand-written answers to one question is precisely the drift class that produced 118 — so the copy is guarded rather than forbidden. This reads the other package's source and fails if they diverge, in BOTH directions, including the fork asymmetry from the other side: adding forked_from here alone would start reporting leopardess's own header as a defect while the code kept serving it. Mutation-proven both ways — narrowing the detector's level list and widening it each COMPILE CLEANLY and each fail with the reason. NOTE A CORRECTION: the first version searched the whole file for each level, and when mutation-tested by narrowing to ('site','header') it reported only 'head' missing — 'footer' passed because that literal appears elsewhere in check_integrity.go as a SLOT NAME. It caught that drift by luck, on the one level with no homonym. It is now scoped to the component_level IN (…) clauses.

grounded_in: link_site_components_action.go, before this change: `if !headerCompID.Valid { if comp, eligible, err := ResolveChromeComponent(ctx, params.DB, ChromeSlotFunction("header"), logger); err == nil && eligible {` — the NULL test is the only gate on the pin, so a present pin never meets the predicate.

site_component_lock_guard.go relinkSiteComponent: `ON CONFLICT (site_id, slot_name) DO UPDATE SET component_id = EXCLUDED.component_id, rendered_html = NULL, build_status = 'pending'` — what the unguarded pin is written into, and why 166's repair is revertible.

component_library.go GetComponentByID, in full: `SELECT id, name, function, COALESCE(category,'') as category, html_template, input_schema, COALESCE(is_dark_section,false) FROM content_components WHERE id = $1 LIMIT 1` — no is_active, no forked_from, no component_level.
